tip: fy (my) triggers nasal mutation: côt becomes nghôt. So fy nghôt means my coat.
o (of) triggers soft mutation: Mehefin becomes Fehefin. The month softens after o in dates.
shw' mae is the south Wales greeting for how are you. The north says sut mae instead.
Welsh puts the verb first: the sentence opens with the verb, then y storm, then y to (the roof).
ei (his) triggers soft mutation: tad becomes dad. So ei dad means his father.
After a number the noun stays singular: pum cannwyll is literally five candle, not candles.
bod carries that in a fact clause: y ffaith bod e yma means the fact that he is here.
dwy is the feminine two and softens the noun: pont becomes bont. dwy bont means two bridges.
sy is the relative verb form for which is or that is: y gardd sy tu ôl means the garden that is behind.
The -ir ending is a passive with no named doer: Cenir means is sung.
The -ach ending makes comparatives, and na means than: gynhesach na means warmer than.
Age uses yn plus oed: naw deg oed means ninety years old, literally ninety of age.
diolch byth is a set phrase for thank goodness, literally thanks ever.
Negatives use ddim after the verb: Dydyn ni ddim means we do not.
gyda becomes gydag before a vowel: gydag un cam means with one step.
Welsh has no verb for need: mae angen X ar Y means Y needs X. angen batri ... ar ei gar is his car needs a battery.
wedi means past when telling time: chwarter wedi dau is quarter past two.
wrth eu bodd is an idiom for delighted, literally at their pleasure.
Welsh shows of by stacking nouns with y between them: Gwlad y gân means land of the song.
tri (three) triggers aspirate mutation: peth becomes pheth. tri pheth means three things.
The echo hi shows ei means her, not his: ei mam hi is her mother.
yn becomes yng before g, and gogledd becomes ngogledd: yng ngogledd means in the north of.
Allwch chi ...? is a polite way to ask can you: Allwch chi siarad means can you speak.
i means to when telling time: ugain munud i bedwar is twenty minutes to four.
Sut wyt ti uses ti, the familiar you for friends and family: it means how are you.
